Something longer has to be split into parts that each fit, or not proposed — a candidate over that ceiling is discarded and the plan comes back missing this part of itself.

Shape: backcountry

Going to: Parc national de la Gaspésie
Dates: 3 nights somewhere between 2027-08-15 and 2027-09-15
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 34, 36
Access needs: not answered
Budget: shoestring, as a feeling rather than a figure
Appetite for effort: demanding
Roughest night they will accept: rustic
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that requires a river ford above the knee

About this backcountry:
Nights away from a road: 3
Shelter: hut
Most they will walk in a day: 16 km
Experience: some
In their words: We have done hut-to-hut in the Chic-Chocs once before, in fair weather. Neither of us has navigated in cloud and we would rather not learn on this trip.

to.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie Discovery Centre

candidatesAccepted.title: Sépaq backcountry huts, Mont Albert / Mont Jacques-Cartier area
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rustic huts and shelters in the park's alpine and forest interior fit a hut-to-hut plan for two, with walking days kept within 16 km. Not answered: access needs. Confirm the current hut list, stage lengths and any ford crossings with the park before booking. Cloud-navigation risk favours the marked, lower-elevation stages.

place.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie backcountry huts

candidatesAccepted.title: Rustic cabin or camp (kind of place, no premises named)
candidatesAccepted.summary: A rustic cabin or basic campsite near the park entrance works as a fallback or a first or last night close to the road. It is also a lower-effort night if weather in the Chic-Chocs closes in. Not answered: access needs.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Albert summit loop via Lac aux Américains
candidatesAccepted.summary: Demanding day hike on the Mont Albert plateau with alpine tundra and cirque views, suited to a 16 km limit. The route is exposed and cloud can arrive fast, so go only in clear forecasts and turn back if visibility drops; access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

place.name: Mont Albert
place.locality: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Sainte-Anne-des-Monts

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit hike
candidatesAccepted.summary: Climb to the highest peak in southern Québec to see woodland caribou habitat and wide views. The summit is exposed with no shelter, so only go in clear weather given the party's wish to avoid navigating in cloud; access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Ernest-Laforce and Lac Paul trail day
candidatesAccepted.summary: A more sheltered, well-marked forested hike that suits a lower-risk day or a poor-weather alternative. Duration and trail details were not verified; access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

place.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie trail network

candidatesAccepted.title: Hut-to-hut leg on the Chic-Chocs sentier international des Appalaches
candidatesAccepted.summary: A single hut-to-hut leg within the 16 km daily limit, matching the party's hut shelter choice and rustic comfort level. Choose a well-marked leg, check conditions with park staff, and note that stream crossings should be checked against the no-ford-above-the-knee limit; hut availability and fees were not verified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Interpretation centre and caribou talk at Gîte du Mont-Albert
candidatesAccepted.summary: A low-effort rest-day stop to learn about the park's caribou and alpine ecology and to check trail and weather conditions with staff before a big day. Opening hours were not verified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Albert plateau loop, huts and alpine tundra
candidatesAccepted.summary: A demanding alpine circuit on the Mont Albert plateau with hut or rustic camping access, suited to a pair with some hut experience. The plateau is exposed and fog is common, so the plan hinges on a clear-weather window; check conditions and trail status with Sépaq (the park's operator) and the park's reception staff, and the Météo-média/Environment Canada mountain forecast. Access needs were not answered, and hut availability and river levels at fords could not be checked, so confirm both locally. This is not clearance to go.

place.name: Mont Albert, Parc national de la Gaspésie

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit, caribou zone
candidatesAccepted.summary: A demanding day on the highest peak in southern Québec, with the summit zone accessible by guided or regulated routes to protect the caribou. It is above treeline with limited shelter, so it should only be done in clear weather, and neither of you has navigated in cloud. Check the access rules, shuttle availability and forecast with Sépaq. This is not clearance to go.

place.name: Mont Jacques-Cartier, Parc national de la Gaspésie

candidatesAccepted.title: Sentier International des Appalaches forest-section hut stay
candidatesAccepted.summary: A lower-elevation, treed section of the trail, which is much easier to follow without cloud navigation skills than the open plateaus and offers a fallback when the tops are clouded in. Check hut booking, trail conditions and river levels with Sépaq. Access needs were not answered and fords cannot be assessed from here. This is not clearance to go.

place.name: Chic-Chocs forest trails, Parc national de la Gaspésie

candidatesAccepted.title: Sépaq backcountry hut and site reservation
candidatesAccepted.summary: Huts and backcountry sites in Parc national de la Gaspésie (Chic-Chocs, incl. Mont Albert and Mont Jacques-Cartier areas) are reserved through Sépaq and often fill for late August; availability, fees and current trail status are unverified here. Access needs were not answered, so nothing here accounts for them. This is not clearance to go.

candidatesAccepted.title: Travel insurance with backcountry rescue cover
candidatesAccepted.summary: Evacuation from remote terrain can be costly, so check that a policy covers hiking in remote areas and medical evacuation, and read its exclusions. Provincial health coverage and any access needs are not answered and not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Offline maps and satellite messenger for cloud days
candidatesAccepted.summary: You have not navigated in cloud and want to avoid learning on this trip, so consider a rented or borrowed satellite messenger, a charged GPS or phone with offline topo maps, and a park-staff check on trail markings and weather before setting out. Cell coverage in the Chic-Chocs is patchy and I could not verify it. Rental options and prices are unknown.

place.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie visitor centre

candidatesAccepted.title: Park shuttle or rental car for trailhead access
candidatesAccepted.summary: Getting from Québec City to the park and between trailheads may need a rental car or a shuttle, and the schedule and prices are unverified. Hut trips often start and end at different points, so check how you get back to your vehicle. Driver licence and age rules were not checked.
